newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on host of bearish factors.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on host of bearish factors.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower in moderate to heavy volume on a mixture of seasonal harvest pressure, spillover weakness from a drop in CBOT soybeans and fund selling, traders said.

"We are now starting to see some harvest pressure, and certainly the limit-down performance in soybeans and the weak wheat market in Chicago forced the hand of traders here," a KCBT trader said before the close.
Wheat drew hedge pressure as harvesting progressed in northern Texas after a two-week delay. Traders said they expected to see cutting progress into Oklahoma by the weekend.
Soybeans dropped sharply and nearby July settled down its daily 30-cent per bushel trading limit on news Cargill Inc was importing soybeans from Brazil to the United States.
KCBT July wheat managed to end firmer than its counterpart in Chicago because, as one trader said, "the fund-selling tapered off here toward the close but the funds kept selling in Chicago late."
KCBT wheat settled 2-1/2 to five cents lower, with July down 5-3/4 cents at $3.76-3/4 per bushel. September lost 2-1/2 cents to close at $3.80.
Refco and E. D. & F. Man International were featured fund-related sellers, with Refco shedding 4.4 million July bushels and one million Sept. Man sold four million July.
Traders said they saw healthy commercial buying on the breaks. Continental Grain bought picked up one million July and two million Sept bushels.
